content.text:
The drawing shows a 10,11-dihydro-5H-dibenzo[a,d]cycloheptene core with an imidazol-1-yl group on C5 and two chlorines on one benzo ring.

**Core.** The left benzene ring is unsubstituted. The seven-membered ring contains the CH2CH2 bridge at the top and the CH carrying the imidazole at the bottom. The right benzene ring is fused to the seven-membered ring.

**Right ring.** Its vertices are:
- C_a (808,620), attached to the CH2
- C (908,620), a CH
- C (958,706), bearing Cl
- C (908,792), a CH
- C (808,792), bearing Cl
- C_b (758,706), attached to the CH(N)

The Cl at (808,792) sits on the carbon adjacent to C_b, which is the carbon next to the ring fusion on the CH(N) side. The other Cl is on the carbon para to C_b's neighbour, i.e. meta to C_a.

**Imidazole.** It is attached through N1. N1 connects to CH=CH and to a CH that is double-bonded to the second N (N3), which closes the ring.

**SMILES.** Starting from the CH carrying the imidazole:

C1(n2ccnc2)c3ccccc3CCc4cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c14

Checking the right ring in this SMILES: c4 (C_a), c (CH), c(Cl), c (CH), c(Cl), c14 (C_b). This matches the drawing, with C_b closing back to the CH and the Cl on the carbon adjacent to C_b.

SMILES: Clc1cc2CCc3ccccc3C(n3ccnc3)c2c(Cl)c1
